test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 03 May 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Maya bought a TV for Rs. 7980 including GST of 14%. What is the original cost of the TV without GST?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total percentage including GST = 100% + 14% = 114%

Given: 114% of original cost = Rs. 7980

1% of original cost = 7980 ÷ 114 = 70

100% (Original Cost) = 70 × 100 = 7000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Price including GST = Rs. 7980

GST Rate = 14%

Formula Used: Selling Price = Original Price × (1 + GST Rate / 100)

 
 Original Cost (100%)
 
 GST (14%)
 
• 
 Total = Rs. 7980 (114%)
 Rs. ?

⇒ 7980 = Original Price × (1 + 14/100)

⇒ 7980 = Original Price × (114/100)

⇒ Original Price = (7980 × 100) ÷ 114

⇒ Original Price = 70 × 100

⇒ Original Price = 7000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

GST Calculation

To find the tax amount only: GST Amount = [Total Price ÷ (100 + GST%)] × GST%.

Percentage Change Base

When a value is increased by r%, the original value is retrieved by dividing the new value by (1 + r/100).

Discount vs Tax

Discount is subtracted from the marked price (MP − D), while GST/Tax is added to the base price (BP + Tax).</p
